subject: Collection hold: unexpected mid-cycle usage spike — evidence & next steps
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia@lucentapps.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Kaur <samira@lucentapps.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-28T09:14:00Z
Subject: Collection hold on account: unexpected usage spike

Jordan —

We just received a notice that our account has been placed on a temporary collection hold due to an unexpected usage spike on 2026-08-27. The billing portal shows ~3.8M extra tokens billed in the mid-cycle window and finance has frozen payments pending investigation (see attached screenshot).

We need:
- A brief explanation for the spike (hourly breakdown + API keys involved)
- Any evidence that those calls were legitimate production traffic vs. replay/backfill
- A timeline for when the hold can be lifted or a provisional credit offered

This is urgent — our EU procurement team (cc'd Samira) needs documentation to lift the payment freeze for internal auditors.

Attachments: billing_hold_notice.png (screenshot from billing portal)

Thanks,
Olivia Chen
Head of Platform, LucentApps
olivia@lucentapps.com
+44 20 7946 0931
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-08-28T11:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Collection hold on account: unexpected usage spike

Hi Olivia — thanks for flagging this and sharing the screenshot. I'm on it. Short plan:

1) Kimberly (billing) will pull the mid-cycle meter and confirm the exact API key(s) and rate windows.
2) Marcus (infra) will run an ingest trace for the suspect window and look for duplicate/replay patterns.
3) I'll coordinate with Finance on a provisional credit if the activity looks like a replay/backfill.

Can you confirm whether Lucent ran any backfill or ingestion jobs on 2026-08-27 (internal batch jobs, replays from staging, or new deployments)? If possible, send top-10 request IDs or the job id. That will speed up matching.

I attached a quick sample export we can start with — will update once Marcus/Kimberly have findings.

Attachments: prelim-usage-sample.csv

— Jordan Blake

Hi all — I pulled the invoice window and meter. A few points and requests to make matching faster:

- Metering is keyed to API key + model variant + timestamp. We can provide an hourly token export for the 2026-08-26 to 2026-08-28 window showing API key attribution.
- Common causes we see: backfills using prod key, replaying queued jobs, or a sudden change in concurrency from a new deploy.
- To correlate we need the exact API key(s) (partial redaction is fine: last 6 chars), and any internal job ids that Lucent used for batch uploads.

If the activity is a replay/backfill we can propose a provisional credit for duplicate requests (subject to confirmation). If it’s true production traffic, we’ll need to follow normal invoice reconciliation.

I attached a short metering guidance doc (fields we'll include in the export). Please provide the API key partials and any request id list.

Attachments: metering-guidance.pdf

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Billing & Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-30T13:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Collection hold on account: unexpected usage spike

Olivia / Jordan — I finished the ingest trace for 2026-08-27 02:00–06:00 UTC. Findings:

- We matched 11 of the 12 request ids you provided to duplicate ingestion attempts during 03:18–03:26 UTC.
- The pattern shows a backfill job that retried each batch 1–2 times due to transient upstream timeouts; retries were counted as separate requests and were not collapsed by our prefix dedupe (the calls had unique request ids each retry).
- The API key in use for that window matches your production key (partial match confirmed via last 6 chars).

Suggested remediation and next steps:
1) Offer a provisional credit for duplicate requests: we estimate ~3.2M tokens were duplicates (prelim calc attached). We can apply this as a one-time credit to clear the collection hold while Lucent completes your internal postmortem.
2) Technical mitigation: we can enable a short-term replay-detection rule scoped to your API key to prevent similar duplicate counts for 72 hours while you roll out a fix.
3) VAT/tax handling: because this is an adjustment inside the same billing period, our finance team will issue a credit memo and a corrected invoice showing EU VAT adjustments; please confirm whether Lucent prefers a net invoice correction or a separate credit line.

Attachments: ingest-trace-20260828.jsonl (extract), provisional-credit-20260830.xlsx
Related link: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-doc-id-for-evidence

If you confirm acceptance of the provisional credit, I'll route the DocuSign for an approval signature and Kimberly will queue the credit memo.

— Marcus Lin
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
